thread:
maya: Quick heads-up — profiler snapshot (A100, batch=1..8) shows a latency crossover around seq_len=384 where decode path outperforms prefill. Also seeing KV cache warmup spikes on the first decode step.

jonathan: Paste the numbers? which kernels are we comparing and what hardware?

maya: Tested on A100-40GB, stock kernels. Summary (p50 latency ms):
```
seq_len | prefill_kv_packed | decode_fused_attn | notes
------:|------------------:|------------------:|------
64     |  14.2             | 16.8              | prefill wins
128    |  22.1             | 24.5              | prefill wins
256    |  36.7             | 37.9              | almost even
384    |  53.9             | 48.3              | crossover
512    |  78.4             | 62.7              | decode wins
```
kv-warmup: first decode step latency spike ~2x at seq_len>=256 when prefix not cached

samir: Interesting. Do we know whether the prefill kernel is suffering from fragmentation or extra memcpy at larger slens? Any SM utilization traces?

maya: I pulled Nsight flame for 384 and 512. Prefill shows longer kernel queuing + more memcpy streams during KV packing. decode_fused_attn has a heavier compute kernel but fewer mem ops.

olivia: Could be the "packed KV layout" code path doing per-batch packing for wider attention windows. If packing complexity scales ~O(seqlen * hidden/warp) it might flip point.

kevin: Also check batching heuristics. If autotuner picks prefill for combined small+mid buckets we might be crossing due to an aggregate batch shape mix. What were the batch sizes?

maya: Batches 1..8 in the synthetic runner. Worst-case for prefill at 512 was batch=4 where the pack step amplified.

arjun: Hypothesis: our routing threshold currently set at 320. With that hysteresis we keep prefill for 320..384 and we hit the slow path before the crossover. We should either tighten the threshold or add a narrowband bucket for 320..448 routing to decode.

jonathan: Can we avoid flip-flopping? We need hysteresis. Maybe three-band: short (<=256)->prefill, mid (257-448)->narrow decode-preferred with higher cost cap, long(>448)->decode. Also add safety: don't switch per-request more than once per 5s for same model to avoid thrashing.

samir: Agreed. Also add KV warmup hint: if request indicates cached prefix present use prefill even if slen in crossover range. If not cached, prefer decode. That should reduce first-step spikes.

olivia: Implementation note: make the routing decision depend on two signals: seq_len and kv_cache_state (WARM/COLD). Weight them: score = alpha*norm_slen + beta*(kvcold ? 1 : 0). Tune alpha/beta with autotune.

kevin: We have autotune telemetry already (per-route scoring). We should add a validation job to sweep alpha in [0.6,1.5] and beta in [0.5,2.0] and measure p95 and p99 across workloads. Want me to spin it up?

maya: Yes please. Also log the kernel selection decisions in trace context so we can correlate chosen kernel -> observed latency per request. Add tags: selected_kernel, slen, kv_state, batch_size.

perf-bot: perf-job:job-879 queued — running sweep alpha=[0.6..1.5] beta=[0.5..2.0] across sampleset=prod-ish-2026-03. Expect ~3h.

arjun: One more edge: prefetch vs on-the-fly KV population. If we prefill KV eagerly we pay upfront but later decode becomes cheap. For interactive workloads that abort early, eager prefill wastes cycles. Maybe make prefill conditional on request intent or estimated output tokens.

jonathan: Good call. Add an "expected_output_tokens" header in examples and emulate in sweep. If expected_output_tokens>32 prefer prefill; else prefer decode. That should be another signal in the autotuner.

samir: Also found a tiny regression in recent kernel update: fused_attention_v2 changed memory layout for keys which increases packing time by ~8% for seqlen 320..480. Reverting that micro-optimization for packed KV could help.

maya: Can you link the PR?

samir: https://git.internal/redwood/eng-runtime/pull/4521 (commented). It has the perf diffs in the description.

olivia: Action items:
- [kevin] run autotune sweep (alpha/beta + expected_output_tokens signal) and attach p50/p95/p99 by slen bucket
- [samir] bisect fused_attention_v2 change and try a variant that preserves old KV packing for prefill
- [maya] add trace tags and kv_state to router logs (short-term sampling only)
- [arjun] propose three-band routing thresholds + hysteresis policy (no more than 1 switch per 5s per model)

kevin: Started autotune (job-879). Will push interim dashboard in #eng-runtime in ~2h.

maya: If autotune shows narrowband decode wins 320..448, let's ship a hotfix to routing config with immediate canary (10% traffic) and monitor p99 and error rates.

jonathan: Also sanity-check memory pressure on A100 when switching to decode for midband — if it increases OOM risk, bump to smaller canary and add fallback to prefill with mem-check.

maya: Sounds good. I'll open a small canary run plan. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

perf-bot: perf-job:job-879 completed — results uploaded to https://perf.internal/runs/879 (summary: decode-preferred midband reduces p95 by 12% for conversational set).

maya: Nice. Let's regroup after kevin posts dashboard and samir posts bisect findings.
